transfer.stem: Which plan preserves the order, visible clue and service limits?
transfer.passage:
Checking an order and a repair
Our school sale raised money for new books. We did not yet know whether all the books had been bought. Students also received a discount on museum tickets, but no discount rate was given. A used desk was described as a real bargain: it was a good buy, not necessarily free.
We placed an order for five replacement wheels. The order did not prove delivery. A customer returned a damaged lamp, but no refund result was recorded. A repair service included a safety check; that did not guarantee that every possible fault had already been fixed.
Before another purchase, we compared two fictional fabric samples. The left sample had neat continuous stitches. The right had a visible gap and loose thread ends, so it needed closer inspection. A small picture could not guarantee the quality of a whole product. Finally, a simple repair restored a bicycle's value without stating a selling price.

options.text: Order five replacement wheels without assuming delivery; inspect the broken stitching; keep the safety check separate from a guarantee that all faults are fixed.
Order five replacement wheels and assume delivery is complete; inspect the broken stitching; keep the safety check separate from a guarantee.
Order five meals; inspect the broken stitching; keep the safety check separate from a guarantee.
Order five replacement wheels without assuming delivery; inspect the broken stitching; assume the safety check proves all faults are fixed.

answer.display: Order five replacement wheels without assuming delivery; inspect the broken stitching; keep the safety check separate from a guarantee that all faults are fixed.
